full_judgment:
2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that the writ-petitioner took loan from the respondent No. 2, Agrani Bank Ltd. Laldighi East Branch, Chittagong long before. That due to some unfavorable circumstances the writ-petitioner could not repay the loan as per stipulations and requested the banks to allow it to make payment installments and the bank also accepted that prayer and made an agreement, but subsequently; without complying with that agreement the bank on 08.02.1998 issued a notice upon the writ-petitioner asking it to pay TK. 9,378,38,735.03/-. Against that notice the writ-petitioner filed writ petition No. 1427 of 1998 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule and also an order staying operation of that notice. Thereafter, in the year, 2003 the writ-petitioner itself filed a money suit No.13 of 2003 in the 1st Commercial Court, Chitagong claiming TK. 16,57,23, 3000.00 as compensation against the bank. The said money suit was subsequently transferred to the Court of 3rd Joint District Judge, Chittagong and was re-numbered as 83 of 2003. The Bank also instituted Mortgaged Suit No. 92 of 2003 which was subsequently re-numberless Artha Rin Suit No. 43 of 2003 against the writ petitioner for realization of outstanding loan amounting to TK. 21,01,03,665.30/-. The writ-petitioner then filed another writ Petition No. 6667 of 2003 in the High Court Division challenging the proceeding of that Artha Rin Suit and obtained Rule and also an order of staying the proceeding of that Artha Rin Suit No.43 of 2003. But subsequently, on the prayer of the writ-petitioner Mills the respondent Bank agreed to waive interest to some extend and informed the writ-petitioner Mills by the letter No. অব্যালাপূশা/ঋণ/১২০৬/০৪ dated 30.10.2004 that it would accept a total amount of TK. 799.63 only after waiver of interest from the writ-petitioner on two main conditions that firstly the Mills would pay TK. 50 laces within 6 months from receipt of that letter and secondly the respondent amount would have to be paid in quarterly installments in 5 years time. It was also stipulated in that letter that firstly the Mills would withdrawn the Money Suit No. 13 of 2000 and also made the rules issued in Writ Petition Nos. 1427 of 1998 and Writ Petition No. 6667 of 2003 discharged for non prosecution and secondly, a compromise decree would be .obtained in Artha Rin Suit No. 43 of 2003 by filing a solenama. The writ-petitioner Mills accepted those conditions of the letter, Annexurc-B, for getting waiver of interest and made down payment of TK. 50 lacs and some installments and also withdrew Money Suit No. 13 of 2000 and caused the Rules issued in Writ Petition Nos. 1427 of 1998 and 6667 of 2003 discharged for non-prosecution. The further case of the writ-petitioner is that the solenama which the Bank drafted for filing in Artha Rin Suit No. 43 of 2003 as per stipulation was not in accordance with the letter, Annexurc-B that it contains an additional condition which was not in that letter. The petitioner requested the respondent Bank to draft the solenarna in accordance with the terms of the agreement stated in their letter, Annexure-B, but did not get any result and thus, the petitioner has been compelled to come to the High Court Division. 

 3. Mr. Abdur Razzaq, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division acted unlawfully in summarily rejecting Writ Petition No. 359 of 2008 inasmuch as it failed to appreciate that the writ-petitioner accepted the terms and conditions given by the respondent No. 2 for obtaining the waiver of interest and payment of total amount of TK. 3,17,50,000.00 including the down payment of TK. 50 lacs and also withdrew Money Suit No. 13 of 2000 and caused the Rules issued in Writ Petition Nos. 1427 of 1998 and 667 of 2003 discharged for non-prosecution; that the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are under a legal obligation to obtain a compromise decree in accordance with the terms of the agreement dated 30.10.2004 in the Artha Rin Suit No. 43 of 2003 by filing a solenama in the Court of Respondent No. 3 and in the premises; that the direction given by the respondent no. 1 upon the respondent No. 2 Bank by the letter dated 24.09.2006 for restoration of the suit is illegal and arbitrary. The learned Counsel further submitted that respondent No. 2 is carrying on the proceedings of Artha Rin Suit No. 43 of 2003 without filing the agreed solenama in the Court of respondent No. 3. The learned Counsel also submitted that the respondent No. 3 is not entitled to proceed with Artha kin. Suit No. 43 of 2003 due to the earlier promises of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 upon which the petitioners relied and acted upon hilly.
